summary: First-run e2e testing of Fish It Automation MVP. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests pass after fixing one 500-error bug in GET /api/telegram/status. Frontend: landing, register, login, auth persistence, dashboard nav, config CRUD, admin page all render and function correctly.

minor.issue: Operator precedence in guard 'not cfg or not cfg.get(group_username) and not cfg.get(bot_username)' is correct but fragile — recommend explicit parentheses for readability.

critical_code_review_comments: telegram_manager.get_meta returned updated_at=None when no session doc existed, causing TelegramSessionMeta pydantic validation to raise 500. Fixed by omitting the field when absent so the model default is used.

automation_engine loops for a user with no Telegram credentials will fire 'ValueError: API ID / API Hash belum di-set' repeatedly in logs when /start is called — this is expected but consider suppressing/rate-limiting the traceback and reflecting a clean paused state (last_error in AutomationState).
test_credentials: Admin: admin@fishit.app / Admin@Fishit2026 (seeded). New users registered on-the-fly with uuid-based emails.
seed_data_creation: Created ~10 disposable test users via /api/auth/register during pytest runs (visible in admin table).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Real Telegram MTProto flows (send-code/verify) were NOT tested (requires real phone). All non-Telegram-runtime endpoints tested. Config save persists correctly; admin RBAC enforced (non-admin gets 403; admin nav link renders). Consider adding /api/admin/users/{id} DELETE endpoint if user deletion is needed (currently only PUT).
rca of the issue: GET /api/telegram/status returned HTTP 500 for any user without a telegram_sessions doc. Cause: TelegramManager.get_meta() returned {'updated_at': None} when doc was missing, but TelegramSessionMeta.updated_at is typed as str (with default_factory=utcnow_iso). FastAPI response_model validation rejected None. Fix: only include 'updated_at' in the returned dict when a stored value exists; else let the pydantic default (current UTC ISO) apply. Verified with pytest after fix (test_status passes).
